adultGuidance: Say each word slowly together, then let your child split it and read the parts one at a time. Listen for the vowel sounds, since every syllable has one. If a word feels hard, cover one part and read the part you can see, then put the word back together. Keep it light and stop while it is still fun.
description: Split printed two-syllable words into syllables and read them, count syllables by listening for vowel sounds, and read two-syllable words in short sentences.
learningFocus: Split a compound word into its two parts, read each part, then read the whole word.
Say a word slowly, listen for the vowel sounds, and count how many syllables it has.
Draw a line to split a two-syllable word, read each part, then read the whole word.
Read short sentences, splitting the two-syllable words as you go.
